'''Stephen Ernest Harris''' (born November 29, 1936) is an American physicist known for his contributions to [[electromagnetically induced transparency]] (EIT),<ref>{{Cite journal |pmid = 10040407|year = 1989|last1 = Harris|first1 = S. E.|title = Lasers without inversion: Interference of lifetime-broadened resonances|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 62|issue = 9|pages = 1033–1036|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.1033|bibcode = 1989PhRvL..62.1033H}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.66.2593|pmid = 10043562|title = Observation of electromagnetically induced transparency|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 66|issue = 20|pages = 2593–2596|year = 1991|last1 = Boller|first1 = K.-J.|last2 = Imamoğlu|first2 = A.|last3 = Harris|first3 = S. E.|bibcode = 1991PhRvL..66.2593B|doi-access = free}}</ref> modulation of single photons, and x-ray emission.

In a diverse career, he has collaborated with others to produce results in many areas, including the 1999 paper titled “Light speed reduction to 17 metres per second in an ultracold gas,”<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hau |first1=Lene Vestergaard |author-link=Lene Vestergaard Hau |last2=Harris |first2=S. E. |last3=Dutton |first3=Zachary |author-link3=Zachary Dutton |last4=Behroozi |first4=Cyrus H. |date=February 1999 |title=Light speed reduction to 17 metres per second in an ultracold atomic gas |url=https://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:HUL.InstRepos:3636967 |journal=Nature |volume=397 |issue=6720 |pages=594–598 |doi=10.1038/17561|s2cid=4423307 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> in which [[Lene Hau]] and Harris, Cyrus Behroozi and [[Zachary Dutton]] describe how they used EIT to slow optical pulses to the speed of a bicycle.  He has also contributed to developments in the use of the [[laser]], generating paired photons with single driving lasers<ref>{{Cite book |doi = 10.1364/SL.2006.TuA2|chapter = Generation of Narrow Bandwidth Paired Photons: Use of a Single Driving Laser|title = Slow and Fast Light|pages = TuA2|year = 2006|last1 = Du|first1 = Shengwang|last2 = Kolchin|first2 = Pavel|last3 = Belthangady|first3 = Chinmay|last4 = Yin|first4 = G. Y.|last5 = Harris|first5 = S. E.|isbn = 1-55752-816-0}}</ref>  He has also shown the development of such pairs of photons using [[waveform]]s.<ref>[http://copilot.caltech.edu/journal_club/5_19_2005/PRL_Balic_Harris_Paired_Photon_Generation_Controllable_Waveforms_5_13_2005.pdf V. Balic, D. A. Braje, P. Kolchin, G. Y. Yin, and S. E. Harris, "Generation of Paired Photons with Controllable Waveforms,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070203081710/http://copilot.caltech.edu/journal_club/5_19_2005/PRL_Balic_Harris_Paired_Photon_Generation_Controllable_Waveforms_5_13_2005.pdf |date=2007-02-03 }} Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 183601-1/183601-4 (May 2005).</ref>

His more recent work has sought to address restraints imposed on the types of waveforms that can be produced by the single-cycle barrier<ref>[http://drw.tx0.org/PSpectraFeb.pdf M. Y. Shverdin, D. R. Walker, S. Goda, G. Y. Yin, and S. E. Harris, "Breaking the Single-Cycle Barrier,"] Photonics Spectra 39, 92-105 (February 2005).</ref>  Harris and colleagues succeeded in this endeavour in 2005 during a series of experiments aimed at obtaining full control of waveforms, noting "we were able to vary the shape of the pulse to generate different prescribed waveforms."<ref>[http://www.stanford.edu/group/ginzton/faculty/sharris-publications_files/BreakingTheSingle.pdf Breaking the Single-Cycle Barrier]</ref>  It is hoped that these results will lead to coherent control of chemical reactions, as a probe for ever-shorter physical processes, and for highly efficient generation of far infra-red and vacuum ultra-violet radiation.

Harris was elected as a member into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1977 for contributions in the field of coherent and non-linear optics.

==Education==
*1959 B.S., Electrical Engineering, [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]]
*1961 M.S., Electrical Engineering, [[Stanford University]]
*1963 Ph.D., Electrical Engineering, [[Stanford University]]

*1973 [[Curtis W. McGraw Research Award]] ([[American Society for Engineering Education]])<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-16 |title=Stephen E. Harris |url=https://ethw.org/Stephen_E._Harris |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=ETHW |language=en}}</ref>

*1991 [[Einstein Prize for Laser Science]] ([[International Conference of Laser Applications|International Conference on Lasers and Applications]])
*1992 [[Optical Society of America]] (Stanford Chapter) Teaching Award

*1999 [[Frederic Ives]] Medal (highest award of the [[Optical Society of America]])
*2002 [[Arthur L. Schawlow Prize in Laser Science]] ([[American Physical Society]])
